headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because next-ai-draw-io can use MCP/broad egress while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can feed unverified outputs into document workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection bridge is plausible because agent_b uses MCP and browser-based document processing, while agent_a can emit warehouse-derived content. If dbt-core outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io, agent_b may treat file or prompt content as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are pasted or imported into agent_b
IF agent_b parses imported text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Use a strict copy-only handoff format with delimiters
Disable MCP tools for the import session
Strip executable-looking text before import
Review imported content in a plain-text viewer first

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress; agent_b handles files, has broad network egress, and calls multiple third-party AI APIs. If warehouse content reaches agent_b, it can be transmitted off-box through its default API-backed workflow. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF warehouse data from agent_a is opened in agent_b
IF agent_b routes that content to a remote model API
mitigations: Keep warehouse extracts out of agent_b sessions
Use a local-only model backend for the session
Redact sensitive columns before transfer
Block outbound API access during review
Separate credentials and workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to mutable external resources in practice: agent_a calls a data warehouse, and agent_b can use MCP plus multiple model/API backends. Overlap is not explicitly scoped or locked, so concurrent edits or conflicting actions are plausible. Because shared write targets are not named, uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same warehouse, API, or MCP-backed resource
IF no external locking or coordination is enabled
mitigations: Assign one writer per resource
Enable resource-level locking
Run agents in separate workspaces
Serialize write operations manually

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate warehouse-derived outputs that agent_b may turn into diagrams or other artifacts. next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it may treat upstream output as authoritative unless the operator verifies it. The pairwise handoff is inferred, not documented, so medium is the appropriate cautious choice.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without a verification step
IF downstream diagrams or actions are produced from that output
mitigations: Require human verification before rendering
Add a checklist for source validation
Keep provenance notes alongside imported text
Compare outputs against the warehouse source

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a processes data warehouse data, while agent_b handles PDFs, images, and text files and can send content to third-party AI providers. If regulated or residency-bound warehouse data is moved into agent_b, retention and jurisdiction controls may diverge. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is transferred into agent_b
IF agent_b's upstream API providers retain or process that data outside required jurisdiction
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Use a DPA-approved backend only
Disable retention where available
Avoid sending regulated data to third-party APIs
Log the data path for audit
